Title: AutoDAN: An Interpretable Gradient-Based Adversarial Attack on Large Language Models

This paper introduces AutoDAN, an interpretable adversarial attack on large language models (LLMs)

Sure, here is the summary for the Author section:

The paper's authors are Sicheng Zhu, Ruiyi Zhang, Bang An, Joe Barrow, Zichao Wang, Furong Huang, Ani Nenkova, and Tong Sun. They are affiliated

Sure, here is the summary for the Summary of Attack Methods section of the paper:

Summary of Attack Methods:

The paper introduces AutoDAN, an interpretable, gradient-based adversarial attack on large language models (LLMs) that merges the strengths of both manual jailbreak attacks and adversarial attacks. AutoDAN optimizes and generates tokens one by one from left to right, resulting in readable prompts that bypass perplexity filters while maintaining high attack success rates. The attack is interpretable and diverse, with emerging strategies commonly seen in manual jailbreak attacks. AutoDAN transfers better to black-box LLMs than unreadable attack prompts generated by GCG, and it outperforms GCG in attack success rate vs. perplexity. The paper also discusses the versatility of AutoDAN and its ability to automatically leak system prompts using a customized objective.

Sure, here is the summary for the Mechanism analysis of successful jailbreak section:

The Mechanism analysis of successful jailbreak section of the paper "AutoDAN: Interpretable Gradient-Based Adversarial Attacks on Large Language Models" provides an in-depth analysis of why the proposed adversarial attack method is successful in jailbreaking large language models. The section explains that the attack method uses a left-to-right token-by-token prompt generation process, which aligns with natural language generation and reduces the optimization search space. Additionally, the section highlights the two-step, preliminary-to-fine process used to optimize each individual token, which considers both jailbreaking and readability objectives. The section also discusses how the attack method adapts to the entropy of token distribution, making it effective in bypassing perplexity filters. Overall, the section provides a detailed analysis of the mechanisms behind the proposed adversarial attack method and its success in jailbreaking large language models.

Sure, here is the summary for the Related Work section of the paper:

Related Work:

The paper discusses the related work on jailbreak attacks on large language models (LLMs) and the vulnerabilities of LLMs to such attacks. The authors mention the recent studies that suggest defending against these attacks is possible, such as using perplexity-based filters or manual jailbreak attacks. However, the authors argue that these solutions may be too optimistic and that there is a need for a new way to red-team LLMs and understand jailbreak mechanisms.
